diagnostic_evidence.quote: has eigenvalues bounded above by $\hat L$

issues.failure_explanation: Lipschitz continuity of the gradient of f(z)=F(Pz) with constant L̂ is equivalent to all eigenvalues of P^T∇²F P lying in [-L̂, L̂], not merely being ≤ L̂. The lemma assumes only twice differentiability, not convexity. For example, F(w)=-100w² has every eigenvalue ≤ 1, yet its gradient is not 1-Lipschitz, so the '⇐' direction of (i) is false. The proof's change of variables is correct, but the final equivalence it asserts is wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'eigenvalues ≤ L̂' with '|eigenvalues| ≤ L̂' (equivalently ‖P^T∇²F P‖₂ ≤ L̂), or add a convexity hypothesis to (i).
issues.overall_effect: Part (i) is false as stated outside the convex case. It remains correct together with M-strong convexity, which is the setting of the global theorems.
issues.title: Lipschitz-gradient characterization uses one-sided eigenvalue bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction to the statement. The global theorems, which assume strong convexity, are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, on the event $\{\tau=\infty\}$, the iterates exhibit conditional geometric convergence in expectation to the noise floor $C$

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality eq:cond-step holds for conditional expectations given F_k. The event Ω_∞={τ=∞} depends on ξ_k, ξ_{k+1}, …, so it is not F_k-measurable. An inequality E[X|F_k] ≤ Y does not imply E[X|F_k, Ω_∞] ≤ Y, so the recursion x_{k+1} ≤ (1-ρ)x_k+ρC under P(·|Ω_∞) is unjustified. Moreover, P(Ω_∞) can be 0 under all the hypotheses (see ISSUE-003), in which case the conditional statement is undefined or vacuous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conditional claim with a truncated-expectation bound. Since {τ>k}∈F_k and F(w_{k+1})≥F_* on N_{r+}⊂U, one gets E[S_{k+1}1_{τ>k+1}] ≤ (1-ρ)E[S_k1_{τ>k}] + ρC P(τ>k). This gives E[(F(w_k)-F_*)1_{τ>k}] ≤ C+(1-ρ)^{k-1}(F(w_1)-F_*-C).
issues.overall_effect: The conditional geometric convergence to the floor C on {τ=∞} in the local nonconvex regime is unproven.
issues.title: Conditioning on the future event {τ=∞} in the fixed-step conditional rate
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument yields a recognizably comparable, though weaker, guarantee type (truncated rather than conditional expectation). No new proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we have used $\mathbf 1_{\{k<\tau\}}\le 1$ to relax the $K$–term.

issues.failure_explanation:
(1-ρ)Y_k ≤ Y_k only when Y_k ≥ 0. When F(w_k)-F_* < C, the drift is positive, so Y_{k∧τ} is not a supermartingale. In addition, after relaxing the K-term the claimed inequality fails for k≥τ, where the bound is Y_k+ρC.

Counterexample: take 1D F=w²/2 and g=w+ζ with ζ~U[-a,a], so μ=μ̂_PL=L̂=α_QG=K_G=1 and K=a²/3. Set r=a/2, r_+=3a/4, ᾱ=1/2, w_1=0. Every hypothesis holds, including ᾱ<3r²/a², and the theorem gives P(τ=∞) ≥ 1. Yet w_3=-ζ_1/4-ζ_2/2 exceeds a/2 with positive probability, and exit in fact occurs almost surely.

failure_location.quote: so $(Y_{k\wedge\tau})_{k\ge1}$ is a supermartingale. Optional stopping at time $\tau\wedge k$ gives

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the infinite-horizon bound with a finite-horizon one or restrict to K=0. For example, use E[S_{k+1}|F_k] ≤ S_k+ρC on {k<τ} to obtain P(τ≤k) ≤ (F(w_1)-F_*+(k-1)ρC)/(α_QG r²/2).
issues.overall_effect: The headline basin-stability guarantee (explicit lower bound on P(τ=∞)) is false whenever K>0. The abstract's and contributions' stability claims are unsupported.
issues.title: False supermartingale claim makes the fixed-step basin-stability bound false
issues.why_classification: The counterexample shows that no infinite-horizon bound of the stated type can hold. The guarantee type must change to finite-horizon or noiseless, which is a major loss of an advertised contribution.

issues.failure_explanation:
Bounding the right side by Y_k requires -mα_k Y_k ≤ 0, i.e. Y_k ≥ 0. This fails whenever F(w_k)-F_* < C̃.

Counterexample: use the same 1D example with β=2.5 and γ=2.5. Then 2 < β ≤ 3.5, α_1=5/7, r=a/2, r_+=6a/7, w_1=0. The theorem gives P(τ=∞) ≥ 1, but w_2=-(5/7)ζ_1 leaves N_r with positive probability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must account for the positive noise drift. For example, use E[S_{k+1}|F_k] ≤ S_k+cα_k² to obtain P(τ=∞) ≥ 1-(F(w_1)-F_*+cΣα_k²)/(α_QG r²/2), which requires a new argument and a weaker bound.
issues.overall_effect: The basin-stability bound in the harmonic-step local theorem is false.
issues.title: Same invalid supermartingale step in the diminishing-step stability bound
issues.why_classification: The stated bound is false and must be replaced by a materially different, noise-dependent bound. This is the loss of a claimed guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: E[1_A E[S_{k+1}|F_k]] = E[1_A S_{k+1}] holds only for A∈F_k. Ω_∞={τ=∞} depends on future noise, so the inequality E[S_{k+1}1_{Ω∞}] ≤ E[(1-mα_k)S_k1_{Ω∞}]+cα_k²P(Ω∞) does not follow. The subsequent division by P(Ω∞) also presumes P(Ω∞)>0, which can fail (see ISSUE-004).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the adapted events {τ>k}∈F_k and S_{k+1}≥0 to prove E[(F(w_k)-F_*)1_{τ>k}] ≤ ν/(γ+k) via the same scalar lemma, and restate the theorem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional O(1/k) rate on {τ=∞} in the local regime is unproven.
issues.title: Multiplying a conditional inequality by a non-adapted indicator 1_{Ω∞}
issues.why_classification: A contained rewrite with adapted indicators preserves the O(1/k) rate in a weaker, truncated-expectation form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under local PL, the fixed learning rate floor is

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated spectrum, tr(H) ≈ 1.1×10³. Deflating the s smallest eigenvalues (all <1) to 1 raises K by less than s·σ²/B, i.e. under 5% for s=50. Meanwhile μ̂_PL rises from 10⁻² to λ_{d-s} (≈0.1 for s=25, ≈1 for s=50), and L̂=10² is unchanged. The paper's floor ᾱL̂K/(2μ̂_PLμ) therefore predicts a 10–100× lower floor; the K increase cannot counterbalance this. Observed modest gains thus contradict, rather than confirm, the predicted product scaling.

failure_location.quote: The two effects counterbalance each other, yielding only modest overall gains, consistent with the predicted noise-floor behavior.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the consistency claim for the right panel and state that the bound overpredicts the gain. Alternatively, compare the observed floors with the exact quadratic stationary loss, which depends essentially only on K.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the quadratic diagnostic validates the 'floor scales with conditioning × noise' design principle is unsupported. The data instead indicate that the floor bound is loose in its condition-number dependence.
issues.title: Diagnostic claim of 'counterbalancing' contradicts the paper's own floor formula
issues.why_classification: The fix withdraws part of the advertised empirical validation of the central design principle; it is more than rewording but requires no new theory.
